sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Yuan Dynasty, 1271 to 1368
sources.note: Direct museum essay, Department of Asian Art, October 2001. Administrative adaptation, southern literati and painting; final paragraph on factionalism, corruption, disasters and rebellion. Avoids its generalization that Mongols had no experience administering complex societies.

sources.title: Columbia University: An Overview of Chinese History
sources.note: Direct indexed university teaching chronology: Yuan 1271 to 1368, Southern Song ends 1279, Beijing capital. The narrative distinguishes dynasty proclamation from completion of conquest.

sources.title: Columbia University: China’s Place in Global History, 1350 to 1550
sources.note: Direct indexed scholarly lecture guide, section II at 10:34. Mongols retreated north while maintaining titles/practices; Ming recruited Mongol administrators and soldiers. Used for qualified continuity, not an exact Northern Yuan termination date.

sources.title: UNESCO: Site of Xanadu
sources.note: Direct Outstanding Universal Value, brief synthesis and Integrity: summer capital, city plan, encampments, hunting enclosure, Tiefan’gan canal and excavated/reburied buildings.

sources.title: Columbia University: Life in China under Mongol Rule, For Peasants
sources.note: Direct paragraphs on fifty-household cooperatives, granaries, surveillance, and compulsory labour. Positive policy descriptions are balanced with their documented burdens, not represented as uniformly successful relief.

sources.title: Francesca Bray: Science, technique, technology in imperial Chinese agriculture
sources.note: Direct full research article, paragraphs associated with footnotes 48 to 65. Wang Zhen 1313, illustrated implements and cotton machinery. Distinguishes recording/dissemination from invention; does not claim every intended transfer succeeded.

sources.title: UNESCO: The Grand Canal
sources.note: Direct description and Outstanding Universal Value. Thirteenth-century network exceeded 2,000 kilometres, with older origins and successive-dynasty development; Caoyun transport and granaries.

sources.title: Marco Polo: Excerpts on China, Columbia primary-source edition
sources.note: Direct three-page PDF, Henry Yule 1903 translation. Page 2, Book II part I chapter XXX coal and bathing, part III chapter LXXV Suzhou silk and paper money. Traveller’s account explicitly attributed; inflated population/bath frequency claims omitted.

sources.title: E. N. Anderson: Cooking with Kublai Khan
sources.note: Direct article by the scholar who co-translated and annotated Yinshan Zhengyao, Flavor and Fortune 19(4), 2012, pages 13 to 14. Uses historical discussion of 1330 court text, not modernized recipe section or unsupported nutritional efficacy.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Recent Acquisitions, A Selection, 2014 to 2016
sources.note: Full indexed original entry, Tray with Women and Boys on a Garden Terrace, object 2015.500.1.31. Fourteenth-century carved red lacquer; two women, twenty-three boys, hide-and-seek, shallow bathing tub, hobbyhorses and pretend official procession. Direct PDF extraction failed; indexed original entry read.

sources.title: British Museum: The David Vases, PDF,B.613
sources.note: Full indexed original object catalogue and curatorial description. Direct fetch failed. 1351 inscription is transcribed in traditional Chinese and translated; 子女平安 appears between 合家清吉 and 至正十一年. Zhang Wenjin’s offering of a pair of vases and incense burner to General Hu Jingyi at Xingyuan temple.

sources.title: National Museum of Korea: Celadon Vase with Fish-like Dragon Handles
sources.note: Full indexed original object catalogue, Sinan6558. Longquan celadon, early-fourteenth-century China-to-Japan merchant wreck, commercial cargo and personal belongings. No exact shipwreck year or artifact total asserted from this entry.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Existing uncovered indexed record, no aliases associated. Broader Mongol Empire has its own card.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: Index 1279 to 1492 circa. Dynasty proclamation 1271, Southern Song end 1279, Yuan rule in China ends 1368. Last period is explicitly a map-coverage warning, not an invented late Yuan phase in China.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: world1279, world1300 and world1400 all repeat bbox [81.255,19.661,141.256,57.599] through 1492. Incompatible with Yuan control in China after 1368; no repair claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: 1351 David vase inscription 子女平安, exact museum transcription, short translation based on museum text. Full indexed original witness; direct museum page inaccessible.
batchIdentityNotes.budget: No reuse of Mongol Empire travel-pass or Khubilai biography sources. Per-URL runtime reuse checked separately. Public quotations below 25 words per source.
